work_completed: In `src/gov/rebuild/command.py` the semantic stage is restored word for word to `w2/integrate`. A failure (endpoint unavailable, hung or failing part way) now gives a successful rebuild with `stores.semantic` = `{"status": "not_recreated", "reason": ...}`, plus the `embedding` note where there is one. The docstring sentence about `REBUILD_FAILED` is gone; the `--seed` paragraph now says only a rebuild whose semantic store is recreated leaves the record. The record (`stores.json`) used to be written under `if embeddings:`; it is now written only under `if stores["semantic"]["status"] == "recreated":`. Otherwise the record removed at the rebuild's start stays removed, so the tree is refused as a base ("no readable record") and nothing is copied from it. This covers seeded runs too. `--no-embeddings` and the rest of the seed are unchanged. It checks the seed answer is `seeded` where seeded, and that there is no record. It checks a seed from that tree into a fresh repository is refused with nothing copied. One more test covers `--no-embeddings`. The unused `GovError` import is removed.

discoveries: (1) `semantic._build` returns `NO_EMBEDDING` from inside `with connection:`, so a part-way failure commits a partial store with its manifest row. Even a cold run whose endpoint is unavailable leaves a manifest, because the row is written before anything is embedded. So the old `if embeddings:` gate plus `manifest() is not None` would have written a warm-base record over partial vectors; this change's gate on `recreated` is what closes that. (2) `TMPDIR=/tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-122` is read-only in the engineer's sandbox (the write allowlist does not include it), so tests run with it put pytest's base temp in the worktree root. (3) The record is still written when only the code graph is `not_recreated`. That was true before this change too and is outside this brief's one change; it means "stores complete" is checked for lexical (which raises) and semantic, but not for the code graph.
risks: A seeded tree whose semantic stage then fails keeps the base's copied vectors plus whatever was embedded before the failure, and answers `not_recreated`. That is the same as at base: no record, so it is never a base. The next full rebuild re-embeds what is missing.
lessons: Engineer briefs should give a TMPDIR that is writable in the engineer's sandbox, for example the session's own `$TMPDIR` or `/home/usain/gov-os-runs/W2-122`, which is on the allowlist; otherwise pytest writes into the worktree and the W2-76 xdist test fails. Stage files by name; the worktree has untracked sandbox placeholders.
